results.scope: Frames compared 0.1s apart on a 160px grayscale copy at 30 fps. Frozen means no 8×8 block changes by 1/255 on average; near-black means mean luma below 7.8%. Single-frame spikes use native-rate adjacent frames, a >3× local baseline and >12/255 block-change floor, with resembling neighbours in the affected block; declared cut edges are omitted from the local baseline. Opening-state candidates compare frame 0 with two following frames; they have no preceding-frame evidence. Nearly uniform means grayscale standard deviation below 1/255 for at least two frames, excluding near-black. Yellow chart markers show pop candidates. Loop checks estimate signed pixel motion, not object trajectories. Grayscale sampling can miss tiny or colour-only defects; the final frame still needs inspection. Evidence only: one small moving detail keeps a frame from counting as frozen, and a moving frame can still feel slow.
